thread.title: Surprise! Pandora posts better-than-expected sales as it gains paying subscribers but why is the stock down?

author: Riley McDermid
title: Surprise! Pandora posts better-than-expected sales as it gains paying subscribers but why is the stock down?
text: – Digital Producer,   22, 2018, 7:32am PST It's a good news/bad news story for Pandora Media and its shareholders. It posted a better-than-expected increase of 63 percent in subscription revenue Wednesday afternoon, boosting its share 11 percent in after-hours trading. Oakland-based Pandora said it had 5.48 million paying subscribers by the end of the fourth quarter, a leap of 25 percent from same time period year-over-year. The company reported revenue of $395.3 million for the quarter vs. $392.6 million during the fourth quarter of 2016, beating analysts expectations. But it missed on its earnings expectations, posting a loss per share of 21 cents, more than the 7 cents analysts had predicted. And its main revenue stream from advertising dropped 5 percent. Alas, the stock dropped 9.5 percent to $4.41 on early morning trading Thursday. Pandora's had a volatile five years, but has made recent steps to attempt to slash costs and streamline its products and focus. Three weeks ago, Pandora Media said that it will cut 5 percent of its workforce and expand its business in Atlanta, because the Southern city is more cost effective than growing the brand in the East Bay. Pandora had around 1,000 employees in the East Bay as of January 2017, according to Business Times research, so a 5 percent cut in the workforce could result in at least 50 fewer jobs. It has introduced multiple layoffs but much of its growth has been hampered by increased competition. The Bay Area internet-radio company also has attempted to diversify via dealmaking; it bought Ticketfly for $450 million in cash and stock in October 2015 in an attempt to take on competitors Spotify and Apple Music (NASDAQ: AAPL).
